_comment: The book's five-tone palette, restated for Mermaid. Improvement #82.
Every value below is one of the five greys in scripts/tex/tokens.tex, converted from
xcolor's lightness to a hex triplet: ink 0.00 -> #000000, inkmid 0.45 -> #737373,
inklight 0.65 -> #a6a6a6, tintone 0.94 -> #f0f0f0, tinttwo 0.88 -> #e0e0e0. Mermaid
has no include mechanism, so this is the one place in the design where a colour is
written twice; if a tint moves in tokens.tex it has to move here too.
Mermaid's default theme is not merely colourful, it is colour-*carried*: a decision
node and a process node differ by hue and by nothing else, and in greyscale they
land within four percent of each other. The shapes carry that distinction on their
own, so every fill here is the same tint and every stroke is full-strength ink --
the same reasoning #81 applied to the three callout types.
fontSize here is only a probe. scripts/lua/mermaid.lua renders each diagram once at
this size to learn how far it will have to shrink to fit the measure, then overrides
the value per diagram so that the shrink lands on \tokDiagramLabelSize. Editing the
number below changes nothing about the printed book; edit the token instead.
The spacings are cut to roughly half of Mermaid's defaults. They are fixed pixel
values rather than multiples of the type size, so on a 1,200px-wide flowchart they
are several hundred pixels of air that the page then pays for by shrinking the type.
Cutting them is the one change that makes a wide diagram more legible rather than
merely smaller.
